Mantle-Blubber Soaker: shared-volume thermal-buoyancy glider with squid burst for silent 1000-m cruise

A theoretical invention designed with Polymath Innovation Studio (https://askpolymath.com), powered by Meta’s frontier Muse models. Not built or tested. Every inspiration and claim comes from a saved investigation whose quotations were checked against their sources.

The brief

A submarine inspired by whales and the living ocean

Must meet:

  • Dives to 1,000 metres
  • Nearly silent
  • Uses little energy

Looked for ideas in: Far fields

Where today’s designs stand

Today's reviewed underwater gliders mostly achieve 1,000 m operational depth with less than 25 kg payload, moving by shifting buoyancy with wings converting vertical motion into forward force. Today's ocean gliders are quiet, buoyancy-driven, long-endurance, profiling autonomous platforms. Across 34 passive-acoustic glider missions, less than 13% of time at sea was unsuitable for acoustic monitoring due to surface communications or glider manoeuvre, leaving the remainder available for analysis. Laboratory biomimetic fin tests show a drag-based system with an additional joint intended to increase thrust and decrease energy input had greater efficiency in low-speed forward movement. How could a design achieve 1,000-metre diving with useful payload while keeping energy use low under weight, size and energy constraints? How could a design achieve near-silent operation while manoeuvring, communicating and sensing without platform-generated and flow noise? How could a design achieve whale-like agile movement at practical speed while preserving long endurance despite slow-movement limits of buoyancy gliding?

Where the ideas came from

Stroke-and-glide buoyancy economy to phase-change thermal buoyancy gliding for quiet 1000-m payloads

Marine mammal diving physiology (living things) → Ocean engineering - thermal-buoyancy underwater gliders (materials/energy harvesting)

Mechanism: deep-diving seals/whales sustain months-long foraging by minimizing stroking. Improving body condition increases buoyancy/lipid store, enabling longer passive glides/drifts and a feedback loop that lowers field metabolic rate to near-basal levels. Transfer: replace muscle + fat + lung compression with wax phase-change + high-ballast thermal buoyancy engine that uses ocean temperature difference to change volume and drive sawtooth up/down glides without continuous propeller power, with aft turbine for hotel-load harvesting. Larger payloads map to body-condition mass: only if housed internally streamlined and near-neutrally buoyant; externally bulky payloads break the economy. Limits: biology uses hypometabolism and compressible gas with no engineering analogue; thermal engine needs surface-deep delta-T, has low power density, and 1000-m pressure/cold/compression effects on wax and hull differ from tissue; silence is inferred from no stroking/pumping, not measured in dB.

Improving blubber condition reduces flipper stroking frequency via positive feedback to lower locomotion cost → High-ballast thermal buoyancy engine trims glider near-neutral to extend unpowered glide phases, reducing pump/propeller dutyAssumes: Extra payload can be made low-drag and near-neutral like blubber, not like external tags; neutral trim is achievable at 1000-m density stratification
Depth-dependent buoyancy from lung compression + lipid enables free prolonged descent/ascent glides → Wax melting/freezing with ocean temperature difference changes displaced volume to drive up/down without shaft powerAssumes: 0-1000 m temperature difference at mission site is sufficient to fully actuate required ballast volume at useful rate
Large non-streamlined instrumentation causes 4x locomotion energy and halved mass gain → Larger glider payloads must be internal/streamlined with uprated ballast capacity, otherwise drag penalty dominates transport costAssumes: Scaling hull for payload preserves lift-to-drag and does not require continuous active pumping that reintroduces noise

Where it may not transfer: Biological economy depends on hypometabolism, compressible lungs/air spaces, and compliant tissue at pressure, none of which transfer to rigid pressure hulls and wax actuators; thermal delta-T in polar/isothermal or deep 1000-m water may be too small/slow, turbine adds drag/noise, and pump/valve transients for high ballast may dominate acoustic signature, while bulky payload drag observed in seals suggests scale-up fails.

“During the short foraging migration, FMR averaged 90.1 (SE = 1.7) kJ kg(-1)d(-1) - only 36 % greater than predicted basal metabolic rate.”6
“Low FMRs in pregnant seals were driven by hypometabolism coupled with a positive feedback loop between improving body condition and reduced flipper stroking frequency.”6
“In contrast, three additional seals carrying large, non-streamlined instrumentation saw a four-fold increase in energy partitioned toward locomotion, resulting in elevated FMRs and only half the mass gain of normally-swimming study animals.”6
“The thermal buoyancy engine changes the buoyancy of the glider, due to the difference of temperature of the ocean, and it drives the glider up and down in the water.”5
“Based on this harvesting mechanism, first, a new type of thermal buoyancy engine with high ballast capacity is presented.”5
“However, the main limitation for their development is their supply of energy.”5

Stroke-Glide Buoyancy Cruising: Narwhal Descent Gliding Mapped to Silent Submarine Transit

Marine Biology - Mammalian Diving Physiology → Ocean Engineering - Underwater Vehicle Depth Control

Narwhals preserve oxygen/endurance by prolonging unpowered glides on descent and reserving active stroking for ascent. Underwater long-endurance platforms achieve the same effect by replacing continuous propeller thrust with variable-buoyancy depth control that trades control agility for energy efficiency. Mapped into a whale-inspired submarine, this becomes a hybrid manoeuvre: brief buoyant/active repositioning followed by long silent unpowered glide with propellers braked/feathered, with passive acoustic sensing scheduled during glides to preserve silence.

Prolonged unpowered gliding during descent, with glide fraction increasing with target depth → Buoyancy-driven sawtooth transit: change buoyancy once, then glide forward-down/up with propeller off, using wings/hull liftAssumes: Submarine has glide-capable hydrodynamics (wings/hull lift) and a low-noise buoyancy engine; assumes transit can tolerate low glide speeds ~0.25-1 m/s average
Low activity preserves oxygen stores and extends submergence; high activity shortens it → Low propulsion/hotel power preserves battery and extends mission; intermittent pumping replaces continuous propeller powerAssumes: Dominant energy cost is propulsion; assumes buoyancy pump energy per cycle is less than continuous propeller energy saved during glide
Foraging tracked by buzzes and spinning; sensing integrated into locomotion cycle → Schedule passive acoustic and ocean sensors to listen/collect during silent glide phases, reserving active pinging/pumping for brief noisy windowsAssumes: Self-noise from pump/propeller is the main detector-limiting noise; assumes mission allows intermittent active sensing

Where it may not transfer: Scale, materials and environment may not transfer: narwhals are ~1-ton air-breathers exploiting compressible lungs/airspaces and muscle efficiency that change buoyancy with depth; a steel submarine at 100s-1000s tons cannot use lung compression, needs heavy pressure-tolerant buoyancy machinery, and buoyancy gliding is slow and current-sensitive. Variable-buoyancy pumps/valves themselves emit transient noise and the PID control study emphasizes trade-offs between energy efficiency and control accuracy, implying poor depth-keeping and manoeuvrability versus propellers.

“Narwhals utilized energy saving measures such as prolonged gliding during descent with increasing target depth but stroked actively throughout the ascent indicating excess oxygen storages.”7
“Deep diving air-breathing species by necessity must balance submergence time and level of exercise during breath-holding: a low activity level preserves oxygen stores and allows longer duration submergence whereas high activity levels consume oxygen quickly and shorten submergence time.”7
“Underwater long-endurance platforms are crucial for continuous oceanic observation, allowing for sustained data collection from a multitude of sensors deployed across diverse underwater environments.”8
“This paper investigates the closed-loop depth control of actuation systems employed in underwater vehicles, focusing on the energy consumption of two different mechanisms: variable buoyancy and propeller actuated devices.”8

Buoyancy-glide cruise with squid-like dual fin plus pulsed-jet burst

Marine biology - cephalopod dual-mode locomotion → Ocean engineering - buoyancy-driven underwater gliders

Squids already combine efficient fins with a pulsed jet in one dual-mode system, with jet-fin coordination tuning faster versus tighter turns. Gliders already achieve ultra-economy by changing buoyancy and using wings for horizontal motion. The invention raw material is a hybrid submarine that cruises as a buoyancy glider and sprints/turns as a squid: fins for low-power cruise/control, pulsed water-jet from a mantle-like chamber for burst and tight turning.

Paired fins for steady swimming and fine control in dual-mode system → Low-power undulating side fins or active wings for cruise and depth-keepingAssumes: Fin thrust principles transfer across scale if Reynolds number and flexibility are re-tuned; assumes deployable fins do not compromise pressure hull
Pulsed jet from mantle cavity for escape, sprint and angular velocity → Through-hull pulsed pump-jet module for sprint and rapid turningAssumes: Mantle volume-change mimicked by rigid pump plus accumulator; assumes short burst duty cycle so energy cost is acceptable
Jet-fin coordination determining faster vs tighter turns → Coordinated control law blending vectored jet pulse timing with asymmetric fin motionAssumes: Kinematic coordination observed in small animals qualitatively transfers to vehicle control; requires new modeling at submarine scale

Where it may not transfer: Scale, materials and environment may not transfer: squid data are from cm-scale muscular-hydrostat animals at shallow depth with intermediate agility; jet propulsion is costly for sustained cruise, and a rigid deep hull cannot deform like mantle tissue while pumping large volumes against high ambient pressure.

“Squids and cuttlefishes are cephalopods with unique muscular hydrostat-driven, dual-mode propulsive systems involving paired fins and a pulsed jet.”10
“which are the lowest measures of R/L reported for any aquatic taxa.”10
“This study indicates that coordination between the jet and fins is important for turning performance, with L. brevis achieving faster turns than S. bandensis and S. bandensis achieving tighter, more controlled turns than L. brevis.”10
“Underwater gliders are autonomous underwater vehicles that profile vertically by changing their buoyancy and use wings to move horizontally.”11

The invention

New vehicle: uncrewed WHALE-MANTLE SOAKER, ~2-5m UUV, rated 1000m, designed for slow sawtooth loiter not sprint. Components and sources: (1) Thermal-blubber ballast from Hou et al. thermal buoyancy engine - wax phase-change + high ballast volume that uses ocean temperature difference to drive up/down. (2) Narwhal glide transit from Tervo et al. + Carneiro et al. variable-buoyancy vs propeller - brief buoyancy change then long propeller-off glide with propeller braked/feathered, passive sensors listen during glide. (3) Seal-condition hull rule from Maresh et al. elephant seals - payload must be internal streamlined near-neutral like blubber, external bulky payload forbidden. (4) Squid mantle fins+jet from Jastrebsky et al. + Rudnick glider wings - paired deployable fins/wings for cruise trim plus mantle-like pulsed water-jet for <5% duty burst turn/sprint. (5) Aft turbine hotel harvesting from Hou et al. How it works: surface warmth melts wax, deep cold freezes it, volume change drives slow 0-1000m glide; wings convert vertical to horizontal; turbine trickle-charges hotel load; fins trim; jet stays sealed except for escape/current/turn. NEW INVENTION beyond sources, not supported: shared-volume mantle principle - same oil/wax circuit acts as SLOW thermal actuator and FAST elastic accumulator: slow thermal charge stored in pressure-compensated elastic mantle bladder, then released as single pulsed-jet squirt via vectored nozzle. Sources show thermal drive, glide economy, and fin+jet separately, never combined in one volume. Conflicts: turbine adds drag vs seal economy; jet discharge pressure pulse and buoyancy-pump transients break silence; large thermal ballast needs large delta-T but 1000-m tropical/polar profiles may be small/slow; fin/hull penetrations vs 100-bar pressure hull; internal-volume fight between wax, accumulator, payload and turbine. SUPPORTED by cited abstracts: buoyancy reduces stroking/propulsion, thermal difference drives motion, variable-buoyancy vs propeller tradeoff, dual fin-jet exists, wings convert buoyancy to horizontal. INVENTION unsupported: shared-volume dual-use, 100-bar elastic mantle, acoustic scheduling gains in dB, net J/m at 1000m with payload.

How the sources become the design

Elephant-seal positive feedback: improving blubber condition reduces flipper stroking frequency to near-basal metabolism → High-ballast thermal-blubber: oversized wax volume trims near-neutral to extend unpowered glide and cut pump/propeller dutyAssumes: Payload can be made blubber-like internal streamlined near-neutral; assumes 0-1000m density stratification and delta-T can actuate required volume at useful rate
Narwhal prolonged descent gliding with depth, low activity preserves oxygen/submergence → Buoyancy sawtooth with propeller braked/feathered, passive listening only during silent glide, active pump/ping in brief noisy windowsAssumes: Propulsion dominates energy; pump energy per cycle < propeller energy saved; assumes mission tolerates 0.25-1 m/s glide and poor depth-keeping vs currents
Squid muscular-hydrostat dual-mode: paired fins for steady/control plus pulsed mantle jet, jet-fin coordination tunes fast vs tight turns → Deployable low-power fins/wings for cruise trim plus through-hull pulsed pump-jet for burst sprint/tight turn under coordinated control lawAssumes: Fin-jet coordination qualitatively transfers if Reynolds/flexibility retuned; assumes rigid pump+accumulator can mimic mantle volume change at 100 bar for short duty cycle
Combined blubber lipid store + mantle cavity volume change in living ocean swimmers → Single oil/wax circuit dual-used for slow thermal buoyancy and fast jet burst via elastic mantle accumulator - slow charge, fast dischargeAssumes: Invention: same fluid/volume can serve both functions without cross-talk; assumes pressure-compensated elastic chamber survives 1000m compression and jet pulse does not erase glide economy or silence

Strongest objection: Scale/materials/environment break each transfer at 1000m submarine scale: seal/narwhal economy relies on compressible lungs, compliant tissue and hypometabolism with no rigid-hull analogue; thermal delta-T over 0-1000m may be too small/slow and wax compresses/loses stroke at 100 bar and cold; squid data are cm-scale shallow muscular hydrostats - rigid hull cannot deform like mantle, jet is inefficient for sustained cruise and pumping large volumes against 100 bar is energy/noise costly with cavitation risk; variable-buoyancy control trades accuracy for efficiency, so glide is slow, current-sensitive, and pump/valve plus turbine drag/noise may dominate; seal 4x penalty for bulky payload suggests any real payload/hull scale-up fails silence and economy.

Verdict: Objection limits to partial transfer, not full silent crewed submarine: plausible only as slow UUV loiter/transit mode with strict duty separation - thermal-buoyancy+fins only for economy, jet only for brief burst - with low-noise pump isolation and internal streamlined payload. Requires direct validation of delta-T actuation rate at site, pump/jet transient noise in dB, and energy-per-meter with payload at 1000m. Current support is abstract-only, not full-text proof and not scientific truth; invention of shared-volume mantle remains untested hypothesis.

Limits of novelty: Novelty claimed only within searches performed: fresh counterevidence search on thermal buoyancy engine deep 1000m pressure limits pump noise energy glider returned 4 unrelated records; fresh prior-work search on whale-inspired submarine silent buoyancy glider squid pulsed jet thermal engine returned zero hits. Parent prior-work searches also returned zero. Empty hits are attempts, not proof of absence. No exhaustive patent/classified review. Evidence is abstract-level snapshots retrieved 2026-11-01, no full-text verification, no calibrated acoustic or J/m numbers; exact-quote check does not establish truth.

Engineering and calculations

POSTULATED hull: 3.2m LOA x 0.45m dia Ti-6Al-4V pressure hull 12mm wall (design choice), 520kg total, <80L internal payload. Calc P=rho*g*h with rho=1025kg/m3,g=9.81m/s2,h=1000m (textbook estimates) => P=10.05 MPa ~100 bar. Design 15MPa => SF1.5. Literature gives no dimensions. POSTULATED thermal-blubber: 25L n-eicosane wax (mp tuned 18-22C, design choice) +15L oil, Al exchangers. Calc dV=25L*0.10=2.5L (10% expansion estimate). F=rho*g*dV=1025*9.81*0.0025=25.1N (~2.56kgf). Glide L/D~4 estimate, vertical 0.3m/s choice => horizontal ~1.0m/s, 1000m dive ~55min. Pump E~314J per reversal. POSTULATED fins+jet+silence: 1.1m carbon wings +2x0.35m fins (design choice); 5L accumulator via 40mm nozzle. Calc T=rho*Q*Ve, Q=0.00167m3/s (5L/3s), Ve=8m/s choices => T=13.7N, impulse ~41Ns, dV~0.08m/s on 520kg for turn. Duty <5% sealed; glide 0.3-0.5m/s silent, listen in glide. SPECULATIVE shared-volume mantle + turbine: same oil/wax circuit slow-charges 5L elastic bladder (polyurethane/aramid 110-bar choice) then fast-discharges via jet; aft 80mm turbine trickle 2-5W hotel estimate. No source shows combined thermal+jet from one volume at 100 bar.

Stress test against the brief

Retrieved abstracts do not establish that a wax thermal engine can drive a 2-5 m vehicle to 1000 m on tropical/polar delta-T; no depth rating, wax type, volume change, or temperature profile was retrieved. Retrieved abstracts do not establish near-silence for thermal-buoyancy glide with stern turbine and pulsed jet; no acoustic levels were retrieved. Slow buoyancy-driven sawtooth glide with wings can be low-energy in principle, but net hotel-power self-sufficiency from a stern turbine is only stated as achievable, not quantified in retrieved text. The shared-volume mantle idea - one oil/wax circuit as both slow thermal actuator and fast elastic pulsed-jet accumulator - is not described in retrieved thermal, glider or squid abstracts, and prior-work searches returned no close combined design.

“The results demonstrate that the proposed controller achieves an average energy consumption reduction of 22% compared to the next most efficient PID-based controller for the VBM-actuated vehicle, though with some impact on control performance.”12
PostulatedThe shared-volume mantle idea - one oil/wax circuit as both slow thermal actuator and fast elastic pulsed-jet accumulator - is not described in retrieved thermal, glider or squid abstracts, and prior-work searches returned no close combined design.510
Working: Hou provides thermal plus turbine, Rudnick provides buoyancy plus wings, Jastrebsky provides fins plus jet; none in retrieved abstracts couples them in one shared volume, so combination is new relative to retrieved set only.
“first, a new type of thermal buoyancy engine with high ballast capacity is presented.”5
“Squids and cuttlefishes are cephalopods with unique muscular hydrostat-driven, dual-mode propulsive systems involving paired fins and a pulsed jet.”10

Limitations:

  • Abstract-only evidence; no full-text wax properties, volume budgets, speed polars, turbine power curves, or acoustic spectra retrieved.
  • Narwhal, seal-condition and wing numbers cited in brief were not retrieved and are unverified here.
  • Prior-work and counterevidence searches were limited; novelty is only within searches performed.
  • Exact quote check does not establish scientific truth or feasibility.

Still to invent

  • What delta-T and wax volume give enough buoyancy for 1000-m sawtooth in tropical vs polar profiles?
  • What is net energy after turbine drag, hotel load, and control actuations?
  • What are radiated-noise levels of buoyancy engine, turbine, and pulsed jet versus listening threshold?
  • Can one fluid circuit meet slow thermal and fast jet requirements at 100 bar without breaking silence or trim?
  • Can 20-30L wax deliver 2-3L stroke fast enough on real profile?
  • Pump/jet transient noise and net hotel with turbine drag?
